title: Longest Rivers in the World
period_label: Flag = where the river ends · Data as of Nov 2026
scope_note: Lengths as published by Encyclopaedia Britannica, to the farthest source where Britannica gives a river-system figure (Mississippi–Missouri, Ob–Irtysh). Exceptions: Murray–Darling uses Geoscience Australia (Britannica gives only its parts); Zambezi and Orinoco use the common figure, as Britannica's is 25%+ off for the same source and mouth. Rivers inside a longer listed system are not repeated; big tributaries are. Flag = country where the river ends (sea, lake or a bigger river).

insights.text: Next: the Colorado. Dams and farms now take so much water it rarely reaches the sea.
Next: the Ganges. It meets the Brahmaputra in Bangladesh and they share one huge delta.
Next: the Danube. It flows through 10 countries on its way to the Black Sea.
The next 3 rivers are only tributaries of the Amazon, yet each is longer than the Danube.
Britannica gives the Mekong 4,350 km. A 2009 satellite survey measured 4,909 km.
In 2008 Brazil's INPE measured the Amazon at 6,992 km. Is the Nile really No. 1?

layout.image_prefer: an iconic, instantly recognisable real photograph of THIS river: the river itself clearly visible as the subject (water, banks, bends, delta or gorge), a famous stretch, city or landmark on its banks; landscape orientation; aerial or elevated views welcome; no maps, no satellite false-colour imagery, no tiny river in a huge landscape

items.name: Nile
items.subtitle: From Burundi's highlands

source.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Nile River
source.quote: a length of about 4,132 miles (6,650 kilometres)

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of river systems by length (revid 1380355572), row 'Nile–White Nile–Kagera–Nyabarongo–Mwogo–Rukarara'

cross_check_2.name: Liu et al. 2009, Int. J. Digital Earth 2(1):80-87 (satellite + field survey)

items.notes: Britannica lists the Nile as the longest river. Liu et al. 2009 (satellite + field survey) measured 7,088 km. Brazil's INPE (2008) measured 6,853 km while putting the Amazon at 6,992 km. Basin countries per Britannica: Egypt, Sudan, South Sudan, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, DR Congo, Burundi, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania.
items.image_hint: show the Nile at Aswan with white-sailed feluccas, palms and desert hills, or the Nile through Luxor / Cairo at golden hour; not the Blue Nile Falls alone, not Lake Victoria, not the Amazon; if those exact views are not freely licensed, any sharp, colourful real photo in which this specific river is clearly the subject is acceptable (free licences first: Pexels, Unsplash, Pixabay, Flickr CC BY / CC BY-SA / CC0)

items.name: Amazon
items.subtitle: From the Peruvian Andes

source.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Amazon River
source.quote: at least 4,000 miles (6,400 km) long

cross_check.name: Wikipedia: List of river systems by length (revid 1380355572), row 'Amazon–Ucayali–Tambo–Ene–Mantaro'

cross_check_2.name: Liu et al. 2009, Int. J. Digital Earth 2(1):80-87 (satellite + field survey)

items.notes: Britannica: 'at least 6,400 km', measured from the Ucayali–Apurímac headwaters; length 'open to interpretation'. INPE (Brazil, 2008) gave 6,992 km by placing the mouth south of Marajó Island (Pará estuary); Liu et al. 2009 gave 6,575 km. Britannica says the Amazon carries about one-fifth of all surface runoff on Earth.
